sonnet.problem: Stop 1 already has a drawer-years joke on card 6 (stuck in a junk drawer). Card 9 adds a second one by calling back to being swapped out for a shiny new stamper, which is the start of those drawer years.
sonnet.rule: His drawer years carry a joke at most once per stop.

sonnet.problem: The text promises these things in the future ("They will rebuild", "Strangers will stand and feed your flocks"). The card tells them as if they are happening now: "get rebuilt", "strangers stand and feed", "foreigners plow".
sonnet.rule: A prediction stays a prediction: "God says Tyre will fall," never "Tyre falls."

sonnet.problem: Verse 7 is a promise ("My people will have a double portion", "they will rejoice"). The card says shame and humiliation "get shown the door" as if it is happening now.
sonnet.rule: A prediction stays a prediction: "God says Tyre will fall," never "Tyre falls."

sonnet.problem: The story card says the one rejoicing is "dressed like someone getting ready for one of the biggest days of their life". That sets up and points to the wedding-clothes answer on card 17 (bridegroom and bride dressed up) before the baker has chosen. The text only gives that picture in the "as a bridegroom… as a bride…" part of the same verse.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

sonnet.problem: The blank answer "righteousness" has already appeared on earlier cards in the stop (card 1 "oaks of righteousness", card 16 "robe of righteousness"). The other answers (wisdom, strength) never appeared, so the baker can pick it by elimination.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

sonnet.problem: Multiple choice makes up 6 of the 10 choice cards (cards 2, 4, 10, 13, 15, 17). True or false and fill in the blank have only 2 each, so one type dominates the stop by a wide margin.
sonnet.rule: No type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
